interface.title: ExonViz (web form)
interface.stage_of_work: Interpretation and figure preparation: placing known variants on a transcript's structure and exporting a publication-ready diagram
interface.what_it_is_for: Turn a transcript accession or HGVS variant description into a to-scale exon diagram that shows reading frames, coding and non-coding parts, and coloured variant markers, and download it as an SVG.

data.note: The server works offline and has cached data only for NM_003002.4 (SDHD, real coordinates; reached through NM_003002.4, NG_012337.3(NM_003002.4):c.274G>T and NM_003002.4:r.[274g>u;300del]) and NM_004006.3 (a made-up 10-exon stand-in for DMD). The page normalises transcript input to 'NM_xxx:c.='. Gene names (DMD, SDHD) resolve to Ensembl transcripts (ENST00000357033.9, ENST00000375549.8) that are not in the cache, so they fail with a 'No offline data' banner.

tree.general: Show where variants fall on a transcript's exon structure and reading frames, and export a figure
tree.specific: Render a scaled ExonViz SVG of an SDHD/DMD transcript, with reading-frame notches at the exon ends and HGVS variants marked, adjust it, and download it

features.name: Sequence-description input with normalisation and parse errors
features.general: Type an identifier or a structured description of changes; the tool rewrites it into a standard form, and on a mistake shows where parsing failed and what it expected
features.specific: Type a gene, transcript or HGVS (c./r., single or [a;b] multiple) in Transcript, Submit; the box comes back normalised (NM_004006.3 → NM_004006.3:c.=, DMD → ENST00000357033.9:c.=), or an orange banner gives the parse error or 'no offline data'. The parse position counts the ':c.=' the tool appends, so it can point past what you typed
steps: type an identifier or HGVS description
read the normalised description put back in the box
if an error banner appears, fix the input using its expected-token list

features.name: Scaled exon diagram with reading-frame notches and variant markers
features.general: Draw the segments of a sequence to scale, with joint shapes that encode the reading frame, thin bars for untranslated parts, and coloured markers plus a legend for each change
features.specific: The SVG on the right of the form: exons drawn at px/bp with chevron notches for the reading-frame phase, UTRs as thin bars when Show non-coding is on, variants as pins or bars in the Variant colors with a legend
steps: submit a transcript or variant description
read the notch shapes at the exon ends for the reading-frame phase
read which exon each marker sits in
toggle Show non-coding to compare coding and non-coding parts

features.name: Figure styling panel
features.general: Adjust a figure's size, spacing, wrapping width, colours, labels and marker style, then redraw it
features.specific: Exon height, Drawing scale, Exon gap size, Figure width, Exon color (CSS named or hex; an unrecognised name such as 'notacolor' is accepted without warning and draws the exons black), Variant colors (space-separated list used in order), Show exon number, Variant shape (pin or bar), then Submit
steps: edit size fields (height, scale, gap, width)
edit the exon colour and the variant colour list
toggle exon numbers and pick the marker shape (pin or bar)
press Submit and check the redrawn figure

features.name: Parameterised SVG export link
features.general: Export the current figure as a vector file through a link that records every setting, so it can be shared or reproduced
features.specific: The Download! link is a /draw?... URL that holds all form values; clicking it, or opening the URL directly, downloads <description>.svg (the direct-URL download was checked by reading the file, e.g. NM_004006.3c..svg with exons 3–6, since the page itself does not change)
steps: render the figure with the settings you want
or copy or edit the /draw URL and open it to get a variant of the figure
serves_tasks: Save the figure as a vector file
